content:
Let the sorted lengths be  
\[
a_1\le a_2\le \cdots \le a_{21}.
\]
The condition that any two lengths differ by no more than a factor of 3 means
\[
\frac{a_{21}}{a_1}\le 3.
\]
Consider the 20 consecutive ratios
\[
\frac{a_{2}}{a_1},\frac{a_3}{a_2},\ldots,\frac{a_{21}}{a_{20}}.
\]
Their product is
\[
\frac{a_{21}}{a_1}\le 3.
\]
Thus at least one of these ratios is at most
\[
3^{1/20}.
\]
So there must be two pieces whose lengths differ by no more than a factor of \(3^{1/20}\).

This bound is sharp: take lengths proportional to
\[
1,3^{1/20},3^{2/20},\ldots,3^{20/20},
\]
scaled so their sum is 21. Then every pair has ratio at least \(3^{1/20}\).

Therefore the smallest value is
\[
\boxed{\sqrt[20]{3}}.
\]
